claims.text: Enhanced surface passivation reduces surface atomic diffusion in multi-element nanoparticles.
Reduced surface atomic diffusion suppresses phase segregation.
Surface passivation preserves a metastable, single-phase solid solution during high-temperature catalytic and thermoelectric operation.
The initial nanoparticles can be prepared in a well-mixed, metastable, single-phase state.
Ligand exchange or controlled thermal treatment can reduce nanoparticle surface-defect density without altering bulk composition.
Catalytic and thermoelectric service temperatures are respectively 773–1173 K and 473–1923 K.
Using an inert or controlled atmosphere limits extraneous oxidation effects.
Surface-defect density and passivation-layer integrity mediate surface and near-surface atomic diffusion rates.
Enhanced surface passivation retards atomic mobility at nanoparticle boundaries.
Limiting atomic mobility prevents thermodynamically driven phase segregation and elemental precipitation.
Composition and annealing temperature can govern the scale and nature of phase decomposition in a multi-element alloy.
Passivated nanoparticles will exhibit less phase segregation than untreated controls under identical high-temperature conditions.
Passivation will produce a more uniform elemental distribution.
The proposed mechanism applies when surface diffusion is the dominant contributor to high-temperature phase instability.
Aggressive environmental degradation can overwhelm the stabilizing benefit of a passivation layer.
The magnitude of diffusion reduction and structural stabilization depends on passivation-layer type and quality and on processing variables.
Oxidation kinetics can complicate isolation of the surface-diffusion effect.

contradictions.description: The intervention is intended to reduce surface-defect density, but the baseline is described as having the same microstructural properties. Because surface-defect density is itself a microstructural property, the control cannot remain identical in all microstructural respects while also differing in the proposed mediator.
